geo_headlines: THE WEEK: AI DOUBTS, THEN OIL. S&P 500 7,623.68 (-0.52% Friday, -0.47% week), 2.50% below its October 6 record close; Nasdaq 100 -0.79% on the week after Thursday's -2.9%, its worst day since June (CNBC). The Dow fell 1.23% Friday but rose 0.41% for a third weekly gain. Chips -3.2% on the week. VIX 19.45.

THURSDAY: META AND LAM HIT TECH. Meta beat on revenue ($64.6 billion vs $63.4 billion) and guided higher, but narrowed capex to $135-145 billion; shares fell 7%. Lam fell 12% and Tesla 3% (Investopedia, CNBC). **The 10-year yield fell 19 basis points intraday, the biggest drop since the March 2023 banking crisis, as money moved from stocks to bonds (Yahoo Finance).**

FRIDAY: OIL TO $117. Brent settled $116.72 (+3.1%), up about 6% on the week and the highest since April (WSJ, NYT); December WTI $103.27 (+3.8%). Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters Thursday as Houthi fighting intensified, and Iran said seven tankers were damaged in Hormuz in a single day (Reuters, Al Jazeera). Energy stocks rose 2.5% Friday; gold fell 1.3% to $4,007.90.

IRAN: THREATS UP, NO US STRIKES. A DNI memo says Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel"; US embassies are on alert and non-emergency staff were told to leave Saudi Arabia (CNBC). The administration has vowed to hold off strikes until after the November 3 midterms (CNBC). Saturday Iran's military chief said US warships will not enter the Gulf "under any circumstances" (Al Jazeera).

RATES AND THE FED. 10-year 5.00% (down 9bp on the week), 2-year 4.69%, 30-year 5.33% (Treasury). Jobless claims fell to 194,000, near 57-year lows (Reuters). FedWatch as of Friday 10/23: October hike 7.8% (from 16.6% Tuesday), December 77.2%. Bitcoin $79,557.99 (-1.9% Saturday).

NEXT WEEK: FED AND MEGACAPS. Tuesday: Coca-Cola, Boeing, UPS, then Visa. Wednesday: FOMC decision at 2:00 PM; Alphabet (4:30 PM) and Microsoft (5:30 PM) after the close. Thursday: third-quarter GDP and September PCE at 8:30 AM; Amazon. Friday: employment cost index (CNBC, StockTitan).
client_frame_short: This week the AI worry came back and oil kept climbing. Meta beat on results but its spending plans spooked investors, tech fell sharply Thursday, and bonds rallied hard as money looked for safety. **Then oil jumped to $117 on Friday as attacks around Hormuz and Saudi Arabia hit wartime highs, and the Dow had its worst day of the week.** The S&P 500 ended the week only half a percent lower. Next week brings the Fed, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon. For clients: diversified portfolios did their job again, and plans do not need to change.
client_frame:
If a client calls this weekend, the story is a choppy week that ended almost flat, with oil and AI spending as the two things to watch.

The week: the S&P 500 fell 0.5%, the Nasdaq 100 0.8%, and the Dow rose 0.4% for its third straight weekly gain. Under the surface it was bumpy: Thursday the Nasdaq had its worst day since June after Meta, Lam Research and Tesla reports, and Friday the Dow fell 1.2% as oil jumped.

AI: Meta's results beat expectations, but investors focused on how much it is spending on data centers. The question is not whether AI is growing, it is how fast the spending pays off. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report next week and will add a lot of evidence.

Bonds did their job: on Thursday the 10-year yield had its biggest one-day drop since the 2023 banking scare, which cushioned balanced portfolios. It ended the week at 5.00%. Markets now see a lower chance of more Fed hikes, about 77% for December, down from 92% Monday.

Oil: Brent rose about 6% this week to $116.72, its highest since April. Ship attacks around Hormuz are at wartime highs and Houthi attacks forced Saudi Aramco to evacuate its headquarters. The administration has said it will hold off on new strikes until after the November 3 midterms.

Why it matters: this is a market sorting out AI winners while energy keeps inflation sticky. Diversification across stocks, bonds and real assets handled it.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and let next week's earnings and the Fed inform decisions rather than headlines. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Friday 5.00%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Friday 5.33%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (Friday $116.72). Brent is there; strikes are the missing piece, and the administration says not before November 3.
